Issued at 255 AM EDT Wed Aug 12 2026

Currently-Tonight... KMLB radar imagery shows dry weather over east 
central Florida. GOES-19 satellite imagery and local observations 
indicate clear to partly cloudy skies. Temperatures are currently in 
the mid 70s to low 80s with dew points in the mid to upper 70s. 
Analysis charts show a mid/upper level high over the Gulf with 500mb 
heights at 594dm (90th percentile), as well as a mid/upper level 
trough over the eastern US coast and the western Atlantic. At the
surface, high pressure (~1020mb) is centered over the eastern 
Gulf. Meanwhile, the 00Z XMR sounding indicates drier air than 
normal for this time of year, especially in the mid to upper 
levels.

The airmass is not expected to change much today from the 00Z XMR 
sounding from last night, therefore, the dry air in the mid to upper 
levels is expected to keep rain chances (20-50%) below normal 
today. Isolated to scattered showers and lightning storms are 
forecast to develop in the afternoon and evening as collisions 
occur between west-northwest surface winds, the east coast sea 
breeze, and outflow from previous showers/lightning storms. Rain 
chances diminish by around 8PM. West-northwest winds at 4-8mph are
expected to turn onshore in the afternoon and evening with the 
east coast sea breeze mainly to the south of I-4. Hi-res guidance 
indicates MLCAPE up to 2,000-3,800 J/kg, 0-6km shear up to 
10-30kts, PWATs up to 1.80-2.20", and conditionally unstable mid 
level lapse rates. The aforementioned parameters are sufficient 
for an isolated strong storm or two to develop which are capable 
of frequent lightning, wind gusts up to 30-50mph, and heavy 
rainfall (up to 1-2") if they can overcome the dry air in the 
mid/upper levels. A hot and very humid day is expected with 
afternoon highs in the low to mid 90s. Additionally, a Heat 
Advisory has been issued for all of east central Florida from 10AM
to 8PM for heat index values up to 108-112F degrees. Remember to 
take frequent breaks from the heat, drink plenty of fluids, wear 
light colored clothing, and shift outdoor work away from the 
hottest parts of the day between the hours of 10am to 4pm. Near to
above normal lows in low 70s to near 80F degrees are forecast 
overnight.

Thursday-Saturday... A similar and persistent forecast is expected 
with a continuation of the heat wave through the week with little 
change in the weather pattern. The 500mb ridge is forecast to expand 
as it builds north and east over the Gulf, as well as the southern 
US through Saturday. The mid/upper level trough over the western 
Atlantic will fill as this occurs. 500mb heights over the southern 
US and the state of Florida are forecast to reach the maximum 
percentile (598dm) for this time of year by Friday evening into 
Saturday. Below normal rain chances (30-40% Thursday, 20-50% 
Friday, and 10-40% Saturday) will continue through Saturday with 
mostly dry air in the mid to upper levels. Light west-northwest 
winds at 4-8mph are forecast to back more southerly each day. 
Winds will back onshore (mainly south of I-4) each afternoon and 
evening with the east coast sea breeze. Isolated to scattered 
showers and lightning storms are forecast to develop in the 
afternoons and evenings as collisions occur between sea breezes 
and outflow from previous showers/lightning storms. The potential 
exists for isolated strong storms capable of frequent lightning, 
wind gusts up to 30-50mph, and heavy rainfall (up to 1-3"). Hot 
and humid conditions will continue with afternoon highs in the low
to mid 90s and heat index values near or at Heat Advisory 
criteria (heat index 108F+ degrees). A Heat Advisory is likely to
be issued for at least areas of east central Florida through at 
least Friday. A widespread Moderate to Major HeatRisk with 
widespread Extreme HeatRisk mainly north of the Treasure Coast 
exists each day. A Major and Extreme HeatRisk effects anyone 
without adequate cooling and hydration. 

Sunday-Tuesday... A very persistent forecast is expected with the 
heat wave forecast to continue through the forecast period. 
Ensembles, LREF-clusters, and deterministic models are in good 
agreement that the 500mb ridge will build over the eastern CONUS 
through Sunday before gradually shifting west-southwest on Monday 
into Tuesday. 500mb heights at the maximum percentile (597dm) are 
forecast through at least Sunday. The NBM has the probability of 
temperatures of 95F degrees or greater at 25%-80% each day with the 
greatest probabilities at inland locations west of I-95, as well as 
Stuart and Titusville. Additionally, the probability of a Major 
HeatRisk is likely to very likely for much of east central Florida 
each day; the probability of an Extreme HeatRisk is 20-50% over 
areas of Lake, Orange, Osceola, and Volusia counties each day. More 
information on HeatRisk can be accessed at 
wpc.ncep.noaa.gov/heatrisk. Below normal rain chances are expected
